Before the rise of Islam, the religions in Arabia were diverse, with indigenous Arabian polytheism (idol worship) being the dominant belief system [d1][d5][d6][d9]. This polytheistic landscape included veneration of deities like Hubal, al-Lāt, al-‘Uzzā, and Manāt at local shrines such as the Kaaba in Mecca [d1][d6]. Other religions present included Christianity, Judaism, Zoroastrianism, and Mandaeism, with their influence varying across different regions of the peninsula [d1][d2][d5][d6]. From around the fourth century CE, monotheistic religions like Christianity and Judaism developed further, and some scholarly trends suggest henotheism or monotheism became increasingly prevalent [d1][d5].
